\section*{Multiple Choice Questions (Single correct)}
\textit{Instructions: Select the correct option with a short explanation.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=Q\arabic*.]
\item \duallayerbox{In a standard RNN, what is the primary purpose of the ``hidden state''?}{What stores the final output of the entire sequence?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item To store the final output of the entire sequence.
    \item To act as a memory that carries information from previous time steps
    \item To calculate the loss function for the current word
    \item To normalize the input embeddings
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Why is the Softmax function typically used in the final layer of a Neural Language Model?}{What prevents the gradients from exploding?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item To ensure the output values sum to 1, representing a probability distribution
    \item To prevent the gradients from exploding
    \item To increase the speed of the training process
    \item To allow the model to handle variable-length sequences
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is a key limitation of feed-forward neural networks for NLP tasks?}{Which networks cannot use embeddings?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item They cannot use embeddings
    \item They assume fixed input size and struggle with temporal order
    \item They cannot be trained with gradient descent
    \item They do not use activation functions
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is the purpose of the ``Forward Pass'' in training?}{What updates weights based on the loss?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item To update weights based on the loss
    \item To calculate the predicted output and compute the loss
    \item To unroll the network into a sequence
    \item To calculate the gradient for each parameter
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is true about the weights U, V, and W across different timestamps in an RNN?}{When are weights re-initialized at every step?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item They are randomly re-initialized at every step
    \item They are reused across timestamps
    \item They increase in value as the sequence progresses
    \item Only the output weight V is reused
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Suppose all activation functions in a 3-layer neural network are linear. What is the effective model equivalent to?}{What is equivalent to a deeper network with more representational power?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item A deeper network with more representational power
    \item A single linear model
    \item A recurrent neural network
    \item A decision tree
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{When training an RNN for language modeling using teacher forcing, the model predicts:}{When does the model predict the next word given predicted history?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item The next word given the predicted history
    \item The next word given the ground-truth history
    \item The current word given itself
    \item All words simultaneously
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{In an RNN, the hidden state at time $t$ depends on:}{When does it depend only on the input at time $t$?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Only the input at time $t$
    \item Only the hidden state at time $t-1$
    \item Both the input at time $t$ and the hidden state at time $t-1$
    \item All future inputs
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Consider a neural network layer defined as: $h = f(Wx)$. The input vector $x$ has shape $(n\_0 \textbackslash{}times 1)$, and the output vector $h$ has shape $(n\_1 \textbackslash{}times 1)$. What must be the shape of $W$?}{For $h = f(Wx)$ with $x$ of shape $(n\_0 \textbackslash{}times 1)$ and $h$ of shape $(n\_1 \textbackslash{}times 1)$, which shape is $(n\_0 \textbackslash{}times n\_1)$?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item $(n_0 \times n_1)$
    \item $(n_1 \times n_0)$
    \item $(n_0 \times 1)$
    \item $(1 \times n_1)$
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is the main role of backpropagation in neural network training?}{What computes predictions during inference?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item To compute predictions during inference
    \item To calculate gradients of the loss with respect to parameters
    \item To initialize weights randomly
    \item To normalize input data
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
